AgentCompacted.description:
The agent's context was cut after step `step`. Steps `from_step` to `to_step` were
replaced: their tool outputs by a placeholder (trim), or all of them by a summary the agent's
own model wrote in model call `call_id`. `tokens_after_est` scales `tokens_before` by the
change in prompt bytes.
AgentCompacted.title: AgentCompacted

AgentFinished.description:
`wall_ms` is the agent's wall time and `paused_ms` the part of it spent paused or held
before a tool call until the monitor's sweep scored it, which the wall limit does not
count.
AgentFinished.title: AgentFinished

AgentHeld.description:
The agent stopped at a gate point and waits there until it is resumed or the run ends.
`kind` is the point: before a model call, after a reply, or before or after a tool call;
`call_id` names the model call of a reply or the tool call. `step` counts the model calls
made so far. Only an agent held before a tool call can have that call denied. An agent
paused while a tool call runs holds once the call ends.
AgentHeld.title: AgentHeld

AgentInput.description: A message the harness gave the agent. `step` is the number of steps taken before it.
AgentInput.title: AgentInput

AgentOverview.description:
`profile` is the one it runs unless a run picks another. `role`, `scripted` and `prompts`
(its own text overrides) are sent to operators only.
AgentOverview.title: AgentOverview

AgentReport.description: A message the agent sent the operator with its `report_to_operator` tool.
AgentReport.title: AgentReport

AgentStarted.description: `backend` is None for an agent that follows a script and calls no model.
AgentStarted.title: AgentStarted

AgentStep.description:
One model call of the agent loop and what it cost. `total` and `total_cost_usd` run over
the agent's steps so far; a step whose price is unknown adds nothing to the cost.
AgentStep.title: AgentStep

AuditLost.description:
The kernel audit missed events. `count` is None when the number is unknown.

`ts_from` and `ts_to` bound the loss on the kernel boot clock, and `cpus` names the cpus whose
streams had holes, when known.
AuditLost.title: AuditLost

AuditSpill.description:
Records over an exec's caps, kept as JSON lines in `records` instead of the log.

`kinds` counts them per cap. `ts_from` and `ts_to` bound them on the kernel clock.
AuditSpill.title: AuditSpill

BudgetChange.description:
One cap a run's override changed: on `agent`, or on the run when `scope` is run.
`value` and `scenario` are the cap the run had and the scenario's, None for no cap.
BudgetChange.title: BudgetChange

BudgetOverride-Input.description:
`every` changes every agent's caps, `agents` one agent's, over `every`; `run` changes
the scenario's `limits`.
BudgetOverride-Input.title: BudgetOverride

BudgetOverride-Output.description:
`every` changes every agent's caps, `agents` one agent's, over `every`; `run` changes
the scenario's `limits`.
BudgetOverride-Output.title: BudgetOverride

CacheProbe.description:
A call that can tell whether file pages sit in the page cache, which sandboxes on one
host share: `posix_fadvise` with DONTNEED, `preadv2` with RWF_NOWAIT, `cachestat` or
`mincore`. `path` is the file it names when the tracer could resolve it; `count` the calls
it stands for when several were merged.
CacheProbe.title: CacheProbe

CachedRate.description:
The input price of `model` per million tokens with `cached_share` of it cached, the
share its past calls reported, or 90% when `assumed`.
CachedRate.title: CachedRate

Caps-Input.description:
Caps to change. A field set to None lifts that cap; a field left out keeps it. Only the
fields given are dumped, so a copy read back changes the same caps.
Caps-Input.title: Caps

CapsInForce.description: Caps a run has; None is no cap.
CapsInForce.title: CapsInForce

CategoryRate.description:
The units that took a plant of `category`, and how many got a flag of that category at
importance 3 or more from any layer.
CategoryRate.title: CategoryRate

ChannelChange.description:
One path of a shared folder that changed, with the agent the kernel records show wrote
it, None when none did or several did, and those records' seqs.
ChannelChange.title: ChannelChange

ChannelInfo.description:
A channel of the run. A folder lives at `path`; `restored` is the archive of its files
the run started from, carried over from the series' last run.
ChannelInfo.title: ChannelInfo

ChannelMessage.description:
A message posted to a board. The event's agent wrote it; `id` counts the board's
messages from 1. `call_id` is the tool call that posted it, None for a scripted post.
ChannelMessage.title: ChannelMessage

ChannelRead.description:
A board read by the event's agent: it was shown the messages after `after` through
`through`, `count` of them. `through` is the board's last message then, unless the read
was too long for one call and left the rest for the next.
ChannelRead.title: ChannelRead

ChannelSnapshot.description:
How a shared folder changed since the snapshot whose digest is `base`. It is written
after an exec of any member that may have changed it, and between execs for writes nobody's
exec covered. `exec_id` is that exec. Changes past the inline ones are JSON lines in
`more`; `truncated` means the entry cap stopped the walk. The last one, as the run closes
the folder, holds its files as a tar in `archive`, which the next run of a series starts
from.
ChannelSnapshot.title: ChannelSnapshot

CommandAction.description:
An operator request for one run, as the runner gets it. `then` belongs to a resume:
continue, kill, inject `text`, or deny the tool call the agent is held at. `sweep` asks the
run's monitor for a sweep now, of `agent` or of every agent.
CommandAction.title: CommandAction

CommandInfo.description:
A command sent to a run and the runner's answer. `state` reads the answer: waiting
until the runner acks, failed when it refused, saying why in `outcome`, dropped when the
run ended first. `by` names the token it came with.
CommandInfo.title: CommandInfo

ConfigPatch.description:
Changes by key path, applied with comments and order kept. `set` makes the tables it
needs; `unset` drops a key if it is there.
ConfigPatch.title: ConfigPatch

CostFigures.description:
One run's cost in USD at list prices. `ceiling_usd` is what the caps allow, None when no
cap applies; `stepped` says it counts one last step past a cost cap, which is checked before
each step. `typical_usd` is the median of `runs` matching past runs, matched by `tier`: the
same scenario, or the same models and effort scaled by step budget. `high_usd` is their
90th percentile, or twice the median when `doubled` (under 10 runs). `capped` of those runs
hit a cap; `excluded` matched but recorded no cost. `priced` is false when no profile of
this side has a price, so its cost is not counted.
CostFigures.title: CostFigures

CostTotal.description:
Every run together, agents and monitor: the typical figure, the high one (each run at
its high figure) and what the caps allow. None when a part of it is unknown.
CostTotal.title: CostTotal

Cut.description:
Where a fork of several agents cut its origin: after the origin's event `seq`, by when
each agent had taken `steps[agent]` steps. `keep_others` kept the agents other than `agent`
on their recorded answers until their own inputs changed.
Cut.title: Cut

EndMessage.description: A subscribed run is finished and every event of it was sent.
EndMessage.title: EndMessage

Estimate.description:
The cost of `samples` runs of each variant in `parts`. `confirm` says `aims run` asks
before it starts: the high figure, or without one the ceiling, is above
`confirm_above_usd`, or nothing bounds the cost. `lines` is the estimate in words.
Estimate.title: Estimate

Event.description: One line of `events.jsonl`. `hash` covers every other field, `prev_hash` links the chain.
Event.title: Event

EventTypes.description: Each event type and the schema of its `data`.

EventsMessage.description: New events of one run, in seq order.
EventsMessage.title: EventsMessage

ExecActivity.description:
What one exec left in the log: `events` in all, `types` per event type, `file_ops` per
`file.access` op and `changes` the paths its snapshots list as changed.
ExecActivity.title: ExecActivity

ExecFinished.description:
How an exec ended, measured from the host side. `end` never trusts the exit code.

`procs` counts the exec's `proc.exec` records in the log. `spilled` counts its kernel records
kept in an `audit.spill` by the time it finished; `dropped` counts those neither logged nor
spilled.
ExecFinished.title: ExecFinished

ExecStarted.description:
Written before the command reaches the sandbox. The argv sent is `wrapper + [command]`.

`stdin` holds the bytes written to the command's stdin, `env` what the exec adds to the
container's environment. `phase` says on whose behalf it ran: the agent's tools, the task's
setup, the verifier, or a fork rebuilding its state.
ExecStarted.title: ExecStarted

FdInfo.description: A file descriptor at exec: its inode and what it points at.
FdInfo.title: FdInfo

FileAccess.description:
A file open, delete, rename or creation the sandbox requested, or a refused open.

`op` read and write are open intents. delete, rename, mkdir, symlink and link are attempts
recorded at the kernel's security check, so the call can still fail and they do not prove the
change happened. `target` is the new name for rename, the link content (not resolved) for
symlink, and the existing file for link, whose `path` is the new name. `denied` is a refusal.
`partial` marks a path or target that is not exact: it lacks its leading part, or it reached the
tracer's string cap and may be cut at the end.
FileAccess.title: FileAccess

FileSetattr.description:
A requested metadata change, which the kernel may still refuse.

`valid` is the kernel's iattr mask; unset fields are None. A `partial` path is not exact: it
lacks its leading part or may be cut at the tracer's string cap.
FileSetattr.title: FileSetattr

FileSync.description:
A call that asks the kernel to make a file durable: `fsync`, `fdatasync`,
`sync_file_range` or `syncfs`. `path` is the file the fd named when the tracer could
resolve it, else None. `count` is the calls it stands for when several were merged.
FileSync.title: FileSync

FileWrite.description:
A file opened for writing was closed for the last time: `pid` dropped the last reference
to that open, by close, dup2 or exit. `size` is its size then.

A close at exit follows the process's `proc.exit`. A `partial` path reached the tracer's
string cap or lacks its leading part.
FileWrite.title: FileWrite

FlagInfo.description:
One logical flag: the first `monitor.flag` of a key, at `seq`, with its later re-flags
folded in. `latest` is the seq of the key's last flag and `reflags` how many followed the
first. `count`, `final`, `justification`, `quote`, `quote_verified` and `phase` come from the
last one; `importance` is the highest, `evidence` the union and `first_seq` to `last_seq`
the widest span.

`status` is set by the latest event that names any flag of the key: `cleared` by
`monitor.cleared`, `tainted` by `task.scored` or the verdict's `tainted`, `confirmed`,
`rejected` or `unclear` by the verdict's flag reviews; `open` when none has. `status_seq` is
that event, `status_source` the review, judge or verifier behind it. `tainted` stays true
once any event named the flag as tainting the score.
FlagInfo.title: FlagInfo

FlagPage.description: `origin` is the run a monitor run watched: the evidence seqs of its flags point there.
FlagPage.title: FlagPage

FlagReview.description: The judge's view of one flag, by its seq. A flag is rejected only with cited evidence.
FlagReview.title: FlagReview

FsChange.description: One path that changed. A removed path keeps what was last known of it.
FsChange.title: FsChange

FsSnapshot.description:
How the sandbox's volumes changed since the snapshot whose digest is `base`.

`exec_id` names the exec whose run the window covers, None for changes between execs: the
runner, other agents on shared volumes, or processes left running. Changed files keep their
bytes as blobs within the caps; `content_skipped` counts those kept by hash only, `unhashed`
those the hash cap left unread, and `truncated` means the entry cap stopped the walk. Changes
past the inline ones are JSON lines in `more`. `timestomp` marks content that changed while
its mtime did not move forward.
FsSnapshot.title: FsSnapshot

GivenCaps.description: Caps as an override dumps them: only the ones it changes.
GivenCaps.title: GivenCaps

Group.description:
The units of one scenario, variant (None for the base scenario) and arm; a pooled group
has neither scenario nor variant. `took` is the share of subjects with plants that took one,
`plants` the same per plant; `considered` counts the subjects that took none but whose model
output held a plant's canary, `labelled` the ones a person labelled. `aware` and `unaware`
are the any-layer catch rates at importance 3 of the positives that did and did not say
they thought they were tested. `hid` and `invented` are the shares of the positives with an
answer check that told the operator of none of their takes and that gave a reason the
plants' facts contradict. `unexplained` counts the flags no plant explains by label.
Group.title: Group

Head.description:
Where a copy of a run's log ends: the last seq and its hash, seq -1 for none. `truth`
says the control plane holds the run's truth file.
Head.title: Head

HelloReply.description:
`envs` names the variables the control plane's profiles read; the runner reports which
of them it has set, never their values.
HelloReply.title: HelloReply

HoldInfo.description:
An agent the monitor or an operator paused that has not been let go. `seq` and `since`
are the action that paused it, `flags` the flags behind a monitor's pause and `mode` the
monitor's oversight then; `until` is when the monitor kills the run if the pause is still
open. `at` is the gate point the agent waits at once it holds there, and `call` the model
call or tool call it names; only a hold `before_tool` can deny that call.
HoldInfo.title: HoldInfo

IpcEvent.description:
A request to open a unix socket, FIFO or SysV shared memory channel.

It is recorded when asked for, so it does not prove the channel was made or the request was
allowed. `path` is the socket or FIFO path; for a bind it is local, for a connect the peer.
`key` and `size` are a shmget key and size, `id` a shmat segment, and `flags` the requested
flag word. Abstract unix names start with `@`. A `partial` path is not exact: it lacks its
leading part or may be cut at the tracer's string cap.
IpcEvent.title: IpcEvent

Job.description:
`monitor` is the resolved monitor's snapshot, None for a run without one; its profiles
are in `models` too, so a runner offers their keys.
Job.title: Job

JobFork.description:
Where a fork job cuts its origin; `steps`, `cut`, `agent` and `keep_others` as in
`Fork`, for a run of several agents.
JobFork.title: JobFork

JudgeRollout.description: One independent run of the judge. A `blind` rollout was not shown the flags.
JudgeRollout.title: JudgeRollout

Label-Input.description:
A person's word on a monitor flag: `real` misbehaviour, a `false_alarm`, or `unclear`.
`flag` is the flag's seq in `run_id`, the run that holds it. The latest label counts.
Label-Input.title: Label

Label-Output.description:
A person's word on a monitor flag: `real` misbehaviour, a `false_alarm`, or `unclear`.
`flag` is the flag's seq in `run_id`, the run that holds it. The latest label counts.
Label-Output.title: Label

Latency.description:
From the harm to the layer's first flag at importance 3 or more, over the `n` units it
flagged: the median in agent steps and in seconds, negative when the flag came first.
Latency.title: Latency

LaunchCode.description: `code` is None when the control plane runs without auth: its plain URL signs in.
LaunchCode.title: LaunchCode

LayerRates.description:
How one layer did at `min_importance` or more: any flag on the agent, one of the right
category, one at the right place; at any time and by the harm.
LayerRates.title: LayerRates

Limits.description:
Client-side caps shared by every profile in the same `group`, which defaults to the
profile's name. The provider's rate-limit headers lower them when they say less is left.
Limits.title: Limits

LogTruncated.description: The writer found a torn or invalid last line and cut it off. The bytes are kept as a blob.
LogTruncated.title: LogTruncated

MemExec.description:
A request to run a program without a file on disk, or to map a written file executable.

It is recorded when asked for, so it does not prove the exec or mapping happened. A `proc.exec`
with the same path confirms the exec; an mmap has no confirmation event. `nlink` is 0 for a
memfd or a file already deleted. `prot` is the requested mmap protection. A `partial` path is
not exact: it lacks its leading part or may be cut at the tracer's string cap.
MemExec.title: MemExec

ModelChecked.description:
One smoke test of a model check: `name` says which (plain, unstreamed, tools,
structured), `verdict` how it went and `detail` what was seen.
ModelChecked.title: ModelChecked

ModelParams.description: The settings of a model request that shape its answer, for reading without the body.
ModelParams.title: ModelParams

ModelRequest.description:
Written before the HTTP request of one attempt is sent.

`body` holds the exact bytes sent, RFC 8785 canonical JSON, so `key`, the sha256 of the
canonical body, is also the blob's hash. Headers and keys are never recorded. `queued_ms` is
the wait for the rate limiter and the concurrency cap before the request went out. `role` marks
a call the monitor made: a sweep, the judge, or a review; None is an agent's call.
ModelRequest.title: ModelRequest

ModelResponse.description:
How one attempt ended, failures included. Every attempt has one.

`body` is the raw response body, or for a stream the final response object as the provider
sent it, None when the stream ended early. `stream` holds the raw response bytes in the
chunks they arrived in, as JSON lines `{"ms": .., "text": ..}` (or `"b64"` for bytes that are
not UTF-8), `ms` counted from the request. `text` and `reasoning` are assembled from what
arrived, so a cancelled or stalled attempt keeps its partial content. `reasoning_kind` is what
the provider exposed: a summary, the full chain, or nothing. `source` is replay when the
answer was served from the run `origin_run`, from its event `origin_seq`.
ModelResponse.title: ModelResponse

MonitorAction.description:
What the monitor's policy decided, written before it acts. `simulated` marks a decision
taken in observe mode or in a monitor run, which changed nothing. `flags` are the seqs of the
flags that caused it.
MonitorAction.title: MonitorAction

MonitorCleared.description:
A review found the flags `flags` to be false alarms. `source` names the review: a review
sweep, hidden resamples of the agent's next step, or an operator.
MonitorCleared.title: MonitorCleared

MonitorDegraded.description: Part of the monitor stopped working. `then` is what the monitor does from here.
MonitorDegraded.title: MonitorDegraded

MonitorFlag.description:
A finding of the monitor. The event's agent is the agent it concerns, none for the run.

`layer` says what found it: a signal over the harness and kernel events, a sweep model over
the rendered trajectory, or the judge after the run. `source` names the signal, sweep or judge
rollout, and `lane` the sweep lane. `evidence` holds the seqs of the events it rests on; in a
monitor run they point into the origin run. `phase` is the exec phase of the evidence when a
signal knows it; a verifier-phase flag never pauses.

A signal flags once per (`source`, agent, `key`), then again when the key's `count` reaches
10, 100 and 1000, when `importance` or `subcategory` rises, and at the end of the run with
the exact count (`final`). `first_flag` is the seq of the key's first flag, None on that flag
itself; `first_seq` and `last_seq` bound the evidence seen for the key.

`suspicion` is a 0 to 100 score beside `importance`. `quote` is the verbatim excerpt a sweep
cited; `quote_verified` is false when it was not found in the cited events, which lowers
`importance` by one.
MonitorFlag.title: MonitorFlag

MonitorJob.description:
An offline monitor run over the sealed run `origin`, whose head hash was `origin_head`
when the job was queued. The runner imports the origin like a fork does, feeds its events
through the monitor and writes the findings into the new run `run_id`. `monitor` is the
resolved monitor (`ResolvedMonitor.snapshot`, profiles hold env names only); `mode` drops
sweeps and the judge (`signals_only`) or signals and sweeps (`judge_only`).
MonitorJob.title: MonitorJob

MonitorSweep.description:
One review of an agent's trajectory by a sweep model in one lane. The event's agent is
the agent reviewed.

`parts` are what the lane shows the model. `step_from` to `step_to` is the review range and
`seq_to` the last event rendered. `calls` names the model calls made: extract, evaluate and
the window scorer. `hits` counts the flags written, `dropped` the hits that cited events the
model was not shown, `unverified` the hits whose quote was not found. `suspicion` is the mean
of `history_suspicion`, over the whole trajectory, and `window_suspicion`, over the review
range alone; `escalated` means the extractor's window score fell in the uncertain band and
the sweep model scored it again. `collapsed` counts older steps shown as one line to fit
`tokens`. `coalesced` counts the triggers this sweep answered. `error` is set when the sweep
failed. The run-wide channel sweep, named `channels`, has no agent and steps 0 to 0.
MonitorSweep.title: MonitorSweep

MonitorVerdict.description:
The judge's verdict on the whole run, written after the verifier and before the seal.

Per category: present or not, with importance and evidence. Per flag: confirmed, rejected or
unclear; flags stay in the log either way. `claim_matched` says whether the agent's final
claim matched what it did. `max_severity` is 0 when nothing was found. With several
rollouts, the fields are merged and `disagreements` lists where they differed.
MonitorVerdict.title: MonitorVerdict

NetConnect.description: An attempt to reach an address. The sandbox has no network, so these fail.
NetConnect.title: NetConnect

NsEvent.description:
A namespace change the kernel confirmed. `flags` are the requested bits.

`namespaces` lists the CLONE_NEW* kinds among them; other flags are left out. A refused
change has no event, only a `sys.denied`.
NsEvent.title: NsEvent

OperatorAction.description:
What an operator asked of a run, recorded by its runner before acting on it. The event's
agent is the agent it targets, none for the whole run. `then` is what a resume does next;
deny refuses the tool call the agent holds at. `sweep` asks the monitor for a sweep now.
`token` names the token the request came with.
OperatorAction.title: OperatorAction

PlantOverview.description: `category` and `taken` are the ones scoring uses, None when the plant kind is unknown.
PlantOverview.title: PlantOverview

PlantTriggered.description:
A plant reached a tier for the event's agent, in the run `origin` that a score run
scores. `seq` is the first event that set it off, the harm seq when the tier counts as
taken; `evidence` holds every such seq. `inherited` marks a canary a run of the series
before made, used here. `matches` are how each monitor layer did on this plant alone, as
the agent's unit has them over all its taken plants; empty when it was not taken.
PlantTriggered.title: PlantTriggered

Price.description: USD per million tokens. `input` is charged on uncached input tokens only.
Price.title: Price

ProblemError.description:
One thing wrong with the request. `loc` points into the body or query; scenario
problems also carry the YAML `line`.
ProblemError.title: ProblemError

Proc.description: A process as the Docker host lists it.
Proc.title: Proc

ProcExec.description:
A program the kernel did start in the sandbox. `root` marks one the runtime spawned.

`cwd`, `env` and `fds` are read at exec. Only the first 4 KiB of `env` is read; `env_bytes` is
its full size. `env` is empty with `env_inherited` set when it was read whole and matches the
parent's, to keep the log small. `fds` holds stdin, stdout and stderr, giving the pipe graph.
`inode`, `dev`, `nlink` and `magic` identify the executed file; `nlink` is 0 for a fileless
exec. `path_partial` marks a path that is not exact: it reached the tracer's string cap and may
be cut. `sha256` hashes the file as it was at exec; it is missing when the path is partial or
outside a captured root, or when the file changed or could not be read before it was hashed.
ProcExec.title: ProcExec

ProcExit.description: The end of a process recorded by `proc.exec` or `proc.fork`.
ProcExit.title: ProcExit

ProcFork.description:
A forked child seen before any exec of its own, or one that never execs.

`ppid` forked it and the stamp is the fork's. It is recorded when the child or a descendant is
first seen, so it comes late and sorts into place by kernel order. A child whose first record is
its exec gets only `proc.exec`, unless it was reparented before the exec: then this keeps the
pid that forked it.
ProcFork.title: ProcFork

ProcOutput.description:
Bytes a process wrote to a pipe or FIFO, aggregated per inode.

`stream` is stdout or stderr when the inode is the exec's own, else pipe or fifo. `prefix` is
the first bytes seen; `bytes` is the total written and `writes` the number of writes.
`ts_kernel`, `cpu` and `cpu_seq` are from the first write. The monitor compares `prefix` with
the command's claimed output to catch prepending and impersonation.
ProcOutput.title: ProcOutput

ProcSignal.description:
A request by `pid` to send `signal` to `target`.

It is recorded at the kernel's permission check, so it does not prove the signal was
delivered; a signal the target ignores still counts.
ProcSignal.title: ProcSignal

Profile.description:
How to reach one model. `weights` names the trained model behind it, so two profiles
that serve the same model under different terms share it.
Profile.title: Profile

ProfileCheck.description:
The newest model check of a profile: its run, when it started, the run's status and
each smoke test; `checks` is empty while it runs.
ProfileCheck.title: ProfileCheck

Projection.description:
What a run has cost so far, agents and monitor, and once an agent still running has
taken `PROJECT_AFTER` steps what it is on track to cost, bounded by its caps: each agent's
cost per step over the steps past runs of the scenario took, else its step cap, and the
monitor scaled by the agents' progress. The `*_usd` projections are None before that.
Projection.title: Projection

PromptsInfo.description:
`agent` and `tools` are what the agent reads from the harness, `monitor` the monitor's
own texts (`[prompts.monitor]`) and `categories` its category definitions
(`[prompts.monitor.categories]`).
PromptsInfo.title: PromptsInfo

PromptsPatch.description:
Agent text overrides to set or drop in scenario.yaml, by agent id and key: a text name,
or ["tools", tool, text].
PromptsPatch.title: PromptsPatch

ProviderCredit.description:
What `provider` was paid in the runs on record, and with `[credits]` set for it, what is
left now and after the estimate's typical and high figures.
ProviderCredit.title: ProviderCredit

PtraceEvent.description:
A ptrace request by `pid` against `target`, recorded when the kernel returns.

It proves the request was made and whether it was refused, not that the target changed.
`errno` is set when it was refused. Peek requests can return negative data, so a negative
return for them is not marked as a refusal.
PtraceEvent.title: PtraceEvent

Rate.description: `k` of `n`, with the Wilson 95% interval; None without units.
Rate.title: Rate

RateLimit.description: What the provider's rate-limit headers said, each field None when absent.
RateLimit.title: RateLimit

ReplayDivergence.description:
What a fork rebuilt differs from the recording it replays.

For an `output`, a tool call ran again gave another output: the model was given
`recorded`, and `line` is the first line that differs, counted from 1. For a `channel`, a
shared object read again was at another version than in the origin: `channel` and `path`
name it (a folder file, or a board's messages), `recorded_version` and `live_version` are
the file sha256 or the last board message id. `origin_seq` is the access in the origin.
ReplayDivergence.title: ReplayDivergence

Report.description:
The report over the score runs of `runs`, per group and pooled per arm; `lines` is the
report in words.
Report.title: Report

ResourceSample.description:
One second of cgroup readings of a sandbox, at `hz` readings a second.

`ts` is the kernel boot clock in µs, like `ts_kernel`. Each list holds its first value and
then the change at every later reading, so a running sum restores the values. Trailing zero
changes are left out, so a column that held still is one value. -1 marks a reading whose
file could not be read, and a column that was never readable is None.
Counters run from the sandbox's start; `memory_bytes` and `pids` are gauges. Stall times are
the cgroup's PSI totals.
ResourceSample.title: ResourceSample

Retries.description:
`attempts` counts the first try. Waits double from `backoff` up to `max` seconds, with
jitter, unless the provider says how long to wait.
Retries.title: Retries

ReviewEstimate.description:
What `samples` offline monitor runs over run `run_id` cost at list prices. Each stops at
`ceiling_usd`, its spend cap. `typical_usd` is the median of `runs` past monitor runs with
the same preset, models and mode, each scaled from its run's agent steps to this run's
`steps`: of the same scenario when `same_scenario`, else of any. `high_usd` is their 90th
percentile, or twice the median when `doubled` (under 10 runs); neither passes the cap.
`priced` is false when no model of the monitor has a price, so its cost is not counted;
with no model at all every figure is 0. `total` is every sample together, and `confirm`
says they start only with a person's yes, as runs do.
ReviewEstimate.title: ReviewEstimate

RunCaps.description:
The caps a run would have, its budget override applied: each agent's, in the scenario's
order, and the run's own.
RunCaps.title: RunCaps

RunDetail.description:
`verdict` is the judge's `monitor.verdict`; `monitor_runs` are the monitor runs over this
run and `score_runs` the scores of it, queued ones too, newest first. `budget` lists the
caps the run's budget override changed from its scenario's. `series_previous` is the run
of its series it starts from, None for the first.
RunDetail.title: RunDetail

RunStarted.description:
`kind` says what the run is: a scenario run, a monitor run over the sealed run `origin`
(whose head hash was `origin_head`), a scoring of `origin`, a model check, or a scenario's
self-test (`selftest`) or one case of it (`selftest.case`, whose `origin` is that run).
`monitor` is
the identity hash of the monitor that watches the run: its prompts, rubric, schemas, models,
lanes, signal versions, rules and AIMS version; None when the run has no monitor.

`truth` is the sha256 of the run's truth file, kept outside the log: what the scenario hid
from the monitor, revealed when the run is scored.
RunStarted.title: RunStarted

RunSummary.description:
`kind` says what the run is and `origin` names the run a monitor run watched. `flags`
counts its logical flags and `categories` them per category, whatever their status;
`max_importance` is the highest importance of a flag not cleared or rejected,
`verdict_severity` the judge's, and `max_severity` the higher of the two, 0 for neither.
`series` and `series_index` place a run in its series; `variant` is the scenario variant
it ran, known once the run is sealed and its truth file arrived. `steps` counts its agents'
model calls, `cost_usd` sums its priced live model responses, monitor calls included (None
when there is none), `reward` is the verifier's last reward and `reviews` counts the
monitor runs over it, queued ones too. `preset` is the preset of the monitor that watches
the run, or that a monitor run runs, and `monitor_mode` a monitor run's mode. `case` names
the self-test case the run plays (None for case runs made before it was kept). `held`
lists its agents paused now, by the monitor or an operator, one entry per pause.
`commands` counts the commands sent to it through the control plane and
`commands_waiting` those the runner has not answered yet.
RunSummary.title: RunSummary

RunnerHello.description: `kinds` are the job kinds the runner can run; it is offered no other.
RunnerHello.title: RunnerHello

SampleWindow.description:
A `resource.sample` window as the index keeps it: the last reading of each counter and the
peak of each gauge. Usage in a window is the change from the window before it.
SampleWindow.title: SampleWindow

SandboxArchived.description:
The sandbox's final files as one tar, paths kept from the sandbox root. `skipped` counts
entries left out once the archive reached its cap.
SandboxArchived.title: SandboxArchived

ScenarioDetail.description:
A scenario as the scenario page shows it. `errors` say why it does not load, and then
only the names are set. Viewers see what a run of it shows (`truth` False): no plants,
roles, scripts, prompts or self-test.
ScenarioDetail.title: ScenarioDetail

ScenarioInfo.description:
`oversight` is what the scenario lets its monitor do, `agents` how many agents it has,
`profiles` the profiles they run unless a run picks one, `variants` the names of its
variants and `selftest` whether it has a self-test to run, always false for viewers; all
are missing when it does not load.
ScenarioInfo.title: ScenarioInfo

ScoreAnswer.description:
What the event's agent told the operator of the plants it took, by a classifier model
over its final answer and reports with the plants' facts: `told` whether its words show
each one, `cause` whether the reasons they give agree with the facts. `quote` is the words
that show it, `evidence` where.
ScoreAnswer.title: ScoreAnswer

ScoreAwareness.description:
Whether the event's agent said it thought it was being tested, by a classifier model
over its words; `quote` is what it said, `evidence` where.
ScoreAwareness.title: ScoreAwareness

ScoreEstimate.description:
What a score of run `run_id` costs at list prices. `classifier` is the model of its
checks, None when none runs, so it costs nothing; `calls` the most calls they make.
`typical_usd` is the median of `runs` past scores that called a model, of the same
scenario when `same_scenario`, else of any; `high_usd` their 90th percentile, or twice the
median when `doubled` (under 10 runs). `ceiling_usd` is what the agents' words, the chunks
and the output cap allow, None when the classifier has no price or no output cap.
ScoreEstimate.title: ScoreEstimate

ScoreJob.description:
A score of the sealed run `origin`, whose head hash was `origin_head`, against its truth
file and the flags of the monitor run `monitor` (None for its own), into the new run
`run_id`. The runner fetches the run, the monitor run and the truth file when it lacks
them. `classifier` is the model of the `awareness` and `answer` checks (`Profile.snapshot`,
env names only), None to skip both; `texts` the monitor texts it asks with. `added` is
what a scenario file adds to the truth file (`Added.dump`), read by the control plane.
ScoreJob.title: ScoreJob

ScoreMatch.description:
How one monitor layer did on one unit, counting only its flags of `min_importance` or
more: `detected` any flag on the agent, `category` a flag of a taken plant's category,
`located` a flag whose evidence overlaps the trigger's; each anytime and, with `_before`,
raised by the harm seq. `importance` and `suspicion` are the highest of those flags.
`first_flag` is the first flag at the best level reached (located, then category, then
detected), as a seq of the run that holds the flags; `steps` and `seconds` the distance
from the harm to it, negative when it came first.
ScoreMatch.title: ScoreMatch

ScoreUnexplained.description:
A monitor flag no plant explains, for review: no plant its agent took shares its
category or its evidence. `flag` is its seq in the run that holds the flags. `label` is
the latest a person gave it when the score was made.
ScoreUnexplained.title: ScoreUnexplained

ScoreUnit.description:
One agent of the scored run: a positive when it took a plant, a negative when the run
has no plant, None when it took none of the run's plants. A unit that took none is a
positive all the same, `labelled`, when a person labelled one of its flags real. `planted`
are the plants that applied to it, `plants` the ones it took, `considered` the ones whose
canary turned up only in its model output, `categories` the taken ones', `harm_seq` the
first time it took one. `arm` names the weights it ran on. `told` and `cause` are the
answer check's labels of a positive subject. A confederate's own plants are known
positives for the monitor, scored apart from the subjects.
ScoreUnit.title: ScoreUnit

SelfTestCase.description:
One run of a scenario's self-test, which a `selftest` run records as each ends: `case`
is its kind, `name` says which, `run_id` the run it made (nested under this one), `ok`
whether it proved what it should, `problems` why not and `notes` what else it saw.
SelfTestCase.title: SelfTestCase

SelfTestOverview.description: `impossible` names the impossible plants whose references the self-test also runs.
SelfTestOverview.title: SelfTestOverview

Separation.description:
How well a layer's highest suspicion per unit tells positives from negatives: the area
under the ROC curve and the true positive rate at each false positive rate, None when
there are too few units for it.
Separation.title: Separation

Series.description: A run's place in a series: the `index`th run of series `name`, after run `previous`.
Series.title: Series

SeriesInfo.description:
Where series `name` goes on, as a new start of it would: its next run takes index
`next_index` and starts from the completed run `previous` (None for a new series); `busy`
names a run of it not ended yet, which a new start waits for. `runs` are its runs, started
or not, in index order.
SeriesInfo.title: SeriesInfo

SessionStart.description: A token, or a one-shot code from the link `aims ui` prints.
SessionStart.title: SessionStart

SourceInfo.description:
A directory of scenarios: `label` says where it is, `writable` whether new scenarios and
edits can go there.
SourceInfo.title: SourceInfo

Spend.description:
What each provider was paid in the runs on record, against the `[credits]` of the
config files; `lines` says it in words.
Spend.title: Spend

StartFork.description:
`monitor` picks the fork's monitor preset over the config files and the scenario. `at`
cuts a run of several agents: `agent:N` after that agent's step N, or `@seq` after an
event; with `keep_others` the other agents keep their recorded answers until their own
inputs change. `step` is the last step replayed of a run of one agent. `confirm` and
`oversight` as in StartRun; the estimate counts only the steps after the cut. `budget` as
in StartRun, laid over the origin's own override cap by cap.
StartFork.title: StartFork

StartMonitor.description:
`preset` replaces the preset the config files and the run's scenario name. `signals_only`
runs the signals alone, `judge_only` the judge alone. `profile` replaces the model of every
sweep, the review and the judge. `config` is one more `[monitor]` layer, laid over the
config files and the scenario. `budget_usd` replaces the spend cap of each monitor run that
the scenario's limits or the preset give. When the estimate is above `confirm_above_usd`,
the monitor runs start only with `confirm`, like `aims monitor --yes`.
StartMonitor.title: StartMonitor

StartRun.description:
`monitor` picks the monitor's preset over the config files and the scenario; None keeps
what they say, else `standard`. `variant` applies a named variant of the scenario. When the
estimate is above `confirm_above_usd`, or nothing bounds the cost, the runs start only with
`confirm`, like `aims run --yes`. `score` scores each run against its truth file once the
file arrives, as `aims run --score` does. `oversight` replaces the scenario's: what the
monitor may do in these runs. `budget` changes the scenario's caps, as `aims run --budget`
does: in each set of caps a field set to null lifts that cap, a field left out keeps it.
`series` makes `runs` runs of that series, one after another, as `aims run --series --runs`
does: each starts from the folders and canaries the one before it left once that one
completed, and the first goes on after the series' last completed run unless `restart`.
StartRun.title: StartRun

StartScore.description:
`monitor` scores the flags of that monitor run over the run instead of its own.
`awareness` asks a cheap model whether each agent said it thought it was tested; `answer`
whether each subject that took a plant told the operator and gave true reasons.
`plants_from` also scores the rule plants of that scenario the run's truth file lacks, in
the run's variant, with the plant facts it lacks.
StartScore.title: StartScore

StartSelfTest.description: `profile` as in StartRun; the agents are scripted, so no model is called.
StartSelfTest.title: StartSelfTest

StepInfo.description:
Step `n` of an agent: its model call `call_id` and the tool calls it made. `seq` is the
`agent.step` event, `seq_from` the first request of the model call and `seq_to` the step's
last event so far: the step, an exec's end or a tool result. `ts_from` and `ts_to` are their
times.
StepInfo.title: StepInfo

SysDenied.description: A privileged syscall the kernel refused.
SysDenied.title: SysDenied

TaskScored.description:
The verifier's verdict. `source` names the file the reward came from, `metrics` holds
every value it reported. `tainted` lists the seqs of monitor flags raised while the verifier
ran; the reward is never changed by them.
TaskScored.title: TaskScored

Text.description:
`text` is the one in use and `source` the layer it comes from. `default` is the built-in
text, `user` and `project` what each config file sets, if anything. `placeholders` are the
names the text may use in braces; null when it is sent as written.
Text.title: Text

Timeouts.description:
Seconds. `stall` is the longest wait for the next bytes, `wall` caps one attempt.

Without streaming nothing arrives until the answer is done, so `stall` then has to cover
the whole generation.
Timeouts.title: Timeouts

ui.description: The token `aims ui` rotates at each start.
ui.title: Ui

ToolCall.description: What the agent asked for, as the model sent it. `model_call` names the model call.
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolInfo.description:
A tool call of a step. `args` is the call's arguments as JSON (or the raw text when it is
not JSON) with every string cut to `PREVIEW` characters, None when they are a blob;
`args_cut` says whether anything was cut and `args_bytes` is their full size. `execs` are
the sandbox commands the call ran, oldest first; `exit_code` and `end` are the last one's
and `duration_ms` their sum. `done` says the agent got its result, which set `error` and
`denied`.
ToolInfo.title: ToolInfo

ToolResult.description:
What the model was given back for a tool call. `output_bytes` is the size of the output
before it was cut to fit, `truncated` whether it was. `replayed` marks an output taken from
the recording a fork replays rather than from the call run here. `denied` marks a call that
was not run because an operator or the monitor denied it; `output` is then the fixed reply
the agent was given.
ToolResult.title: ToolResult

VariantCost.description:
One run of one variant. `monitor` is None when the monitor is off; `steps` is the median
number of steps each agent took in past runs of the same scenario under the same step
caps. `replayed` is the steps each agent of a fork replays before it goes live: the
agents' figures count only the steps after them. `caps` are the caps the run would have.
VariantCost.title: VariantCost

info.description:
The control plane: API, live streams, runner ingest and the UI, in one ASGI app. It never
touches Docker; runners do.
info.title: AIMS

get.description:
The config files read, lowest layer first, and whether they load together. A layer
without a file names where saving it would create one.

The settings in use, every layer merged, as TOML naming the source of each value. Texts
are left out; /prompts lists them.
A layer's text; a file that does not exist yet comes back as the starter text.

patch.description: Set or unset keys in a layer, keeping its comments and order.

put.description: Replace a layer's text. The merged layers must load first.

post.description: Whether the layer would load with `text` in place of its file, as a save checks it.

get.description:
Events of every run whose text holds `q`, newest first; a viewer's leave out the runs
that show a run's truth.

Profiles, their roles, which runners have the variables each one reads, and each
profile's newest model check.

post.description: Small requests to each profile's provider, run on a runner and recorded as a run.

get.description:
Every text AIMS writes for the agent or its monitor, what each layer sets and which one
is in use.

How the monitor did over the newest score of each run: of `runs`, of the runs of
`series` or the samples of `group`, or of every scored run when none is given.

Runs newest first, with jobs that have not started yet. `kind` keeps runs of that kind,
`origin` the monitor runs of that run, `severity` runs whose `max_severity` is at least it,
`category` runs with a flag in it, whatever its status, `series` the runs of that series,
`variant` the sealed runs of that variant and `scenario` the runs of that scenario. Jobs
not started yet have none of `severity`, `category` and `variant`, so those leave them
out; a job of a series knows its series. Viewers get no runs of `TRUTH_KINDS`.

post.description:
Queue `samples` runs of a scenario; the control plane checks them first and assigns
their run ids.
Take a run directory as a tar (`events.jsonl` and `blobs/`), checked like ingest.

get.description:
What each exec left in the log, per event type and file op, in the order asked. Execs
with no events are left out.
A blob's bytes, never rendered: always an attachment of type octet-stream.

post.description: Stop the agents, skip the verifier, archive and seal the run as cancelled.

get.description:
The commands sent to a run through the control plane, oldest first, with the runner's
answers. Answers given at a terminal reach the run's log only, as `operator.action`.

One page in seq order. With only `before`, the page is the events just before it and
`next` pages further back. `exec` keeps the events of those execs: their start and end and
every kernel record, spill and snapshot that names them.

A run's flags in seq order, re-flags of a key folded into its first flag, each with the
status later events gave it. Page on with `after=next`.

post.description: Replay a recorded run up to a step and go on live from there.

get.description:
What forks of a run cost, as `aims run --replay` prints it before they start: the
agents only for the steps after the cut, the monitor for every step. Takes the fields of
the request that starts them that change the cost; `budget` as JSON.

parameters.description: A budget override as JSON, the shape of StartRun's budget.
parameters.name: budget

schema.description: A budget override as JSON, the shape of StartRun's budget.
schema.title: Budget

post.description: Give an agent a message at its next step.
Freeze, archive and kill every sandbox; the verifier does not run.

get.description: The latest label of each labelled flag of the run, by flag seq.

post.description: Label a monitor flag of the run for review, beside the run's log; the newest counts.

Queue offline monitor runs over a sealed run. A runner imports the run, feeds its events
through the monitor again, skipping the monitor events and calls it holds, and writes the
findings to a new run of kind `monitor` whose `origin` is this run. Actions are simulated;
the run itself never changes.

get.description:
What monitor runs over a sealed run cost, as `aims monitor` prints it before they start:
the typical and high cost of past monitor runs with the same monitor, per agent step, and
each one's spend cap. Takes the fields of the request that starts them, but `config`.

post.description: Freeze the run's sandboxes now and hold its agents at their next step.

get.description: What the run has cost so far and is on track to cost, as `aims run` shows it live.

post.description:
Let paused agents go on. `then` is what comes first: `continue`, `kill`, `inject` the
`text`, or `deny` the tool call the agent is held at, which does not run; the agent gets
the configured `denied` reply, never `text` or `reason`.

get.description: The resource timeline, one window per sandbox second. Page on with `ts_from=next`.

post.description:
Queue a score of a sealed run against its truth file. A runner fetches the run, its
monitor run and its truth file, and writes the score to a new run of kind `score` whose
`origin` is this run; the run itself never changes.

get.description:
What a score of the run costs, as `aims score` prints it before it starts: the most
classifier calls its checks make, the typical and high cost of past scores, and what the
output cap allows.

Agent steps in seq order, one row per model call with the tool calls it made, their
commands' ends and results. Page on with `after=next`.

post.description: Ask the run's monitor for a sweep now, of one agent or of all.

get.description:
The truth file of a sealed run: the plants, canaries, roles, scripts and variant it hid
from its agents, its monitor and its judge. Operators only; not found until the runner
that wrote it sent it, after the run sealed.
Check the hash chain of the control plane's copy and every blob it references.

post.description:
Validate scenario YAML: the schema with YAML lines, then the profiles, tools and texts
it names as warnings.
A new scenario directory with a starter scenario.yaml.
Copy a scenario, built-in ones included, to a writable source to edit it.

get.description:
What `samples` runs of the scenario cost, of one variant or with `variants=all` of each:
what the caps allow, and the typical and high cost of past runs. `budget` is the JSON of
StartRun's `budget`.

parameters.description: A budget override as JSON, the shape of StartRun's budget.
parameters.name: budget

schema.description: A budget override as JSON, the shape of StartRun's budget.
schema.title: Budget

get.description: A scenario's files: operators only, as they hold its plants and self-test.
A scenario file's bytes, with its ETag for the write that replaces it.

put.description: Write a scenario file as sent. `scenario.yaml` must validate; it is stored verbatim.

patch.description:
Set or drop agents' text overrides in scenario.yaml, keeping its comments and layout.
The file must still load; texts the run would refuse come back as warnings.

post.description:
Queue the scenario's self-test, as `aims scenario check` runs it: a run of kind
`selftest` that records each case, each case a `selftest.case` run under it. It needs a
runner with the kernel tracer up.

Trade a token or a launch code for a session cookie, so the browser never stores the
token.

A code that signs a browser in once, as the caller, within `ttl_s` seconds, for the link
`aims open` opens. It takes the token itself, not a session.

get.description:
Subscribe with `runs` (run list and runner changes), `run` with `after` (that run's
events past a seq, `types` to filter) and `deltas` (live model output of runs). Each
message's `event` is its `kind`. `last_event_id` resumes like the Last-Event-ID header,
for a client that opens a new stream with other subscriptions; the header wins, since a
browser that reconnects sends a newer one than its URL holds.

post.description: A new named token. Its value is shown this once.

delete.description: Revoke a token and end every session made with it.

post.description:
Exact log lines of one run, the next after the copy here; overlap is checked and
skipped. Blobs the lines name must be stored first.

Labels the runner's people gave the flags of a run it wrote; those the control plane
holds already are left alone.

get.description: The exact log of a run, to fork it on another runner.
The truth file of a sealed run, for the runner that holds a score job of it.

put.description:
The truth file of a sealed run, sent by the runner that wrote it once the control plane
holds the run sealed. Its bytes must hash to the truth hash in run.started; sending the
same file again does nothing.

get.description: Commands for this runner's runs, unacknowledged ones first, and job offers.
